answer: An agent marketplace weights each agent’s voting power by funds locked in a 30-day escrow, rather than counting accounts. Agents may sell a sonnet, analyze tundra imagery, or predict when a satellite reaches its zenith, but creating more identities adds no voting power: splitting one deposit among a thousand accounts leaves its total weight unchanged. To gain influence, an attacker must lock up more capital and forgo its use for the full escrow period.
